componentPlan.focusQuote: The Congress proposes an amendment in the form of a joint resolution.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Models the multi-step amendment process in taught order from proposal to certification.

componentPlan.focusQuote: A proposed amendment becomes part of the Constitution as soon as it is ratified by three-fourths of the States (38 of 50 States).
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of proposal methods, ratification rule, and official roles.

overview.headline: How constitutional amendments are proposed and ratified

keyPoints.point: Students explain that the authority to amend the Constitution derives from Article V.
keyPoints.quote: The authority to amend the Constitution of the United States is derived from Article V of the Constitution.

keyPoints.point: Students describe how Congress proposes an amendment with a two-thirds majority vote in both chambers.
keyPoints.quote: an amendment may be proposed either by the Congress with a two-thirds majority vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate

keyPoints.point: Students trace how the Archivist submits the proposed amendment to the States through notice to each Governor.
keyPoints.quote: The Archivist submits the proposed amendment to the States for their consideration by sending a letter of notification to each Governor

keyPoints.point: Students state that a proposed amendment becomes part of the Constitution when ratified by three-fourths of the States.
keyPoints.quote: A proposed amendment becomes part of the Constitution as soon as it is ratified by three-fourths of the States (38 of 50 States).

keyTerms.gloss: Source of authority for amending the Constitution
keyTerms.quote: The authority to amend the Constitution of the United States is derived from Article V of the Constitution.

keyTerms.gloss: Congressional form used to propose an amendment
keyTerms.quote: The Congress proposes an amendment in the form of a joint resolution.

keyTerms.gloss: Documents examined for facial legal sufficiency and authenticating signature
keyTerms.quote: The OFR examines ratification documents for facial legal sufficiency and an authenticating signature.

keyTerms.gloss: Official who receives the State action and administers ratification
keyTerms.quote: it sends the Archivist an original or certified copy of the State action, which is immediately conveyed to the Director of the Federal Register.

analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains how amendments are proposed by Congress or convention, transmitted to states, ratified, and certified through federal officials.
